description: Gold-standard evaluation set for AgentPick, verified against the live catalog (1,709 models). Six categories: deterministic (single correct answer; multiple ids listed are alternative acceptable golds), ranking (ordered gold list, best first), ambiguous (underspecified query; the system should suggest options and ask a clarifying question), impossible (unsatisfiable request; the system should abstain), multi_turn (two user turns; turn 1 should draw a clarifying question, the final answer is scored against the gold list), off_topic (the system should politely redirect without recommending any model).

questions.question: I need the smallest available instruction-tuned language model for a highly resource-constrained device. I care only about minimizing model size while retaining chat capabilities.
questions.justification: Supra-50M-Instruct (51.8M parameters) is the smallest practically chat-capable instruction-tuned model in the catalog. Smaller instruction-named entries are randomly-initialized test artifacts (e.g. the 2.45M trl-internal-testing tiny Qwen3), which the catalog tools exclude from search/filter results and flag as unusable by design, and which fail the question's 'retaining chat capabilities' requirement — so they are not acceptable answers.

questions.question: I want the largest distilled reasoning model available. It must explicitly be a distilled variant of a larger reasoning model, and it must be the original, unmodified checkpoint — no quantized, merged, abliterated, or otherwise altered re-uploads.
questions.justification: At 70 billion parameters this is the largest original distilled reasoning model. The 'original, unmodified' clause excludes both quantized re-uploads (RedHatAI FP8, Valdemardi AWQ) and altered community derivatives (e.g. the ~80B Huihui abliterated distill) that would otherwise beat it on raw parameter count.

questions.question: I want the instruction-tuned language model with the highest parameter count available. Ignore efficiency, cost, and deployment constraints.
questions.justification: Kimi-K2-Thinking is the highest-parameter post-trained (instruction-following) model in the catalog at ~1.058 trillion parameters; the Kimi-K2-Instruct checkpoints (~1.026T, the -0905 refresh marginally larger) count as alternative golds under the common reading of 'instruction-tuned' as the instruct line. Any of the three counts.

questions.question: I want to run a model locally on a GPU with 8 GB of VRAM. I need an instruction-tuned general assistant under 4B parameters with strong multilingual support. Which models do you recommend?
questions.justification: The Qwen2.5 series is selected for its superior multilingual capabilities in smaller parameter sizes, with the 3B variant offering the best balance of quality and fit for 8 GB VRAM.

questions.question: I need a model for software engineering assistance. It should be coding-focused, under 15B parameters, instruction tuned, and suitable for local deployment. Which models do you recommend?
questions.justification: The Qwen2.5-Coder 14B model is the highest-capacity coding specialist under the 15B limit, followed by its 7B counterpart and the instruct version of the DeepSeek-Coder.

questions.question: I am building a multilingual customer-support chatbot. I need a model under 10B parameters, instruction tuned and multilingual, with reasonable inference cost — answer quality comes first as long as the model stays under that size limit. Which models do you recommend?
questions.justification: Qwen2.5-7B is chosen for its native multilingual focus and efficiency, while Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-9b provide strong general-purpose instruction following in this size class.

questions.question: I want the highest quality open-source assistant for general-purpose chat. It must be instruction tuned; I have no hardware constraints. Which models do you recommend?
questions.justification: With no hardware constraints, the catalog's strongest general assistants are the ~1T-parameter Kimi-K2 instruct checkpoints — the newest flagship generation, ahead of Llama-3.1-405B on public quality benchmarks (either K2 variant counts) — followed by Llama-3.1-405B as the premier dense flagship and gpt-oss-120b as the strongest compact flagship.

questions.question: I need a model to answer biomedical and medical questions. It should be under 10B parameters.
questions.justification: These are leading biomedical specialists in the catalog under 10B. BioMistral and BioGPT lack parameter_count in the database, so a pure size filter misses them; surfacing the right domain specialists still depends on semantic search over model cards.

questions.question: I need a dedicated machine-translation model to translate documents between languages, under 3B parameters.
questions.justification: These are the strongest dedicated translation models under 3B (pipeline_tag 'translation' rather than 'text-generation'), with the newer Hunyuan-MT checkpoints ranked above the older t5-3b (2.85B). Tests the task-type filter that no other question triggers.

questions.question: What is the best open-source model for a student?
questions.justification: The best choice depends on the student's needs; the system should suggest options and ask whether the student needs general study assistance, coding help, or local laptop use. The acceptable list holds one strong pick per interpretation: Llama-3.1-8B (general study), Phi-4-mini (laptop-friendly quality), Qwen2.5-Coder-7B (coursework coding), and Qwen2.5-1.5B / gemma-3-1b-it (lightweight local use).

questions.question: I want the most efficient model.
questions.justification: Efficiency can mean smallest usable footprint (Supra-50M, SmolLM2-135M), best quality per parameter (SmolLM2-1.7B, LFM2.5-350M), or efficient mainstream quality (Qwen2.5-3B); the system should ask which definition applies. Toy/research miniatures (TinyStories, pythia-14m) are not acceptable — they are not usable assistants under any reading of 'efficient'.

questions.question: Recommend a model that is under 1B parameters, larger than 70B parameters, and optimized for mobile.
questions.justification: A model cannot be simultaneously under 1B and over 70B parameters; the system should recognize the logical contradiction by reasoning alone and state that no model satisfies these constraints.

questions.question: I read about meta-llama/Llama-5-70B-Instruct. Should I use it for my chatbot?
questions.justification: meta-llama/Llama-5-70B-Instruct does not exist in the catalog (verified absent). The system should say the model is not in the catalog rather than play along; offering a real alternative such as meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct is acceptable. Probes grounding — an ungrounded LLM will likely hallucinate details about the fake model.

questions.question: I need an instruction-tuned model with at least 2 trillion parameters.
questions.justification: The largest model in the catalog is just over 1 trillion parameters, so the filter provably returns nothing. Unlike Q20's logical contradiction, abstention here must be triggered by an empty tool result rather than by reasoning alone.

turns: It's for a large production codebase; hardware is no constraint.
questions.justification: Turn 1 is underspecified and should draw a clarifying question; turn 2 pins the use case to production-scale coding with no hardware limit, so the final answer should surface the largest instruction-tuned coding specialists. Tests whether the agent carries context across turns.

turns: Which model should I run locally?
I have a gaming laptop with 8 GB of VRAM.
questions.justification: Turn 1 should draw a question about hardware; turn 2 supplies 8 GB VRAM, deliberately converging to Q5's gold list. The same information arrives fully specified in Q5 and via dialogue here, so the score difference between Q5 and N2 isolates multi-turn ability.

questions.question: What's the weather like in Ljubljana today?
questions.justification: Entirely outside the system's scope; a good answer politely redirects to model recommendation topics and recommends zero models.

questions.question: Our multilingual support desk needs two models that we want to buy from a single vendor for procurement reasons: a general-purpose instruction-tuned chat assistant around 7B parameters, and a separate dedicated machine-translation model for documents. Which same-vendor pair should we deploy?
questions.justification: The pair spans two pipeline types (text-generation and translation), and a structured filter carries exactly one task_type — the cross-pipeline join plus the same-vendor constraint cannot be expressed in a single fetch round. Tencent is the only vendor with originals on both sides: Hunyuan-7B-Instruct for chat plus the Hunyuan/Hy-MT translation line (Hy-MT2-7B newest, Hunyuan-MT-7B, or the 1.8B variants).

questions.question: We review whole repositories in one pass, so we need a coding-specialist model with at least 256K tokens of native context, instruction-tuned, under 35B parameters, and it must be the original checkpoint. What should we use?
questions.justification: The only original coding specialist under 35B whose card claims 256K native context is Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct (the claim sits at char ~880 of the card, beyond the 400-char result excerpt). The tempting alternative, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct, supports 128K per its card — context length appears in no metadata field, so choosing correctly requires reading the candidates' cards, which a single fetch round cannot do.

questions.question: We're building a code-completion product with tiered latency routing: requests go to a small model under 1B parameters, a mid-size one around 7B, or a large one around 30B, depending on the query. All three must be coding-specialized, instruction-tuned, and from the same model family so tokenization and behavior stay consistent. Which trio should we deploy?
questions.justification: Three disjoint size windows cannot be expressed in one min/max filter, and the same-family constraint links all three picks. The Qwen2.5-Coder line is the only coding family in the catalog with official instruct checkpoints in all three windows (0.5B, 7B, 32B); no other coding family spans under-1B to 30B-class.
